_provenance: Market physics: prices converge, arbitrage creates trade, elasticity matters. The genome IS the DSL numbers; the simulated player is a greedy arbitrageur who reads a wiki. The economy either survives that player or it does not.

walls.top_route_share: No single route MUST dominate the economy. Above 70% means every commodity and station exists but only one pair pays — the market is a corridor, not a network. The DSL's Titanium printer (Titan_Surface -> Orbital_Hub_7, +27/kg, riskless) currently owns the entire economy; this wall is why it is a problem.
walls.routes_used: At least 3 distinct commodity-route pairs MUST be profitable. Fewer than 3 means the greedy player starves on 2/3 of the station graph. The name is DeepSpaceTrader, not OneRouteHauler.
walls.stations_visited: All 3 stations MUST be reachable. Below 3 means some station has zero profitable routes in or out — half the market is a ghost town the player never visits, and the name 'Ares_Market_Central' is a lie.
walls.rate_decay: The best route MUST exhaust itself. rate_decay measures how much the early-game credit rate drops by end-game. Above 0.50 means the economy is a static money printer — the player does the same route forever and it never stops paying. Zero elasticity causes exactly this; the genome MUST discover it needs elasticity.
walls.elasticity: The genome MUST discover price elasticity. The DSL has NONE (elasticity=0.0) — that is precisely why the money printer exists. This wall requires the optimiser to walk away from zero, which is the whole point of making elasticity a reachable locus.
walls.hours_to_next_ship: A second ship MUST be reachable within the 60-hour window. 999.0 is the sentinel meaning it never happened; below that means the economy can eventually afford expansion. The goal is not infinite growth — it is that the economy has a trajectory that is NOT flat starvation.
